mcItems.q: When estimating a causal effect using a natural experiment, what condition must be met for the causal claim to be credible?
op: The two groups must be identical except for the policy change
The groups must be comparable apart from the change
The policy effect is always attributable to the policy
Observational data alone proves the causal effect
mcItems.ex: The causal claim is credible only if the two groups were comparable apart from the change. This comparability is necessary for attributing the effect to the policy rather than a confounding factor.

mcItems.q: Under what circumstance can the effect of a policy change be attributed to the policy rather than a confounding factor?
op: When the two groups are completely identical before the event
When the policy change is the only variable observed
When the two groups were comparable apart from the change
When the effect is observed in a controlled laboratory setting
mcItems.ex: The effect can be attributed to the policy rather than to a confounding factor only when that comparability holds. This condition ensures the policy is the source of the observed difference.

keyTerms.df: A natural experiment employs a policy change or external event affecting one group but not another to estimate a causal effect from observational data.
keyTerms.eg: Researchers used a sudden regulatory shift to estimate the impact on a specific industry.
keyTerms.mi: A natural experiment allows researchers to definitively prove a causal effect without needing any prior knowledge of the groups.
keyTerms.cx: A natural experiment requires that the two groups were comparable apart from the change, not that the effect is definitively proven.

keyTerms.df: The credibility of a causal claim in a natural experiment depends on whether the groups studied were comparable except for the specific policy change.
keyTerms.eg: The study's credibility rests on whether the treatment and control groups shared similar characteristics prior to the intervention.
keyTerms.mi: A causal claim is credible if the observed effect is large and statistically significant.
keyTerms.cx: A causal claim is credible only if the two groups were comparable apart from the change.

The proxy variable eliminates all measurement error.
